abstract: Broadband dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) with widely tunable repetition rates and simplified frequency stabilization is desirable for diverse sensing applications. Here, we demonstrate DCS using two gain-assisted fiber ring resonators that share a continuous-wave (CW) laser and incorporate intracavity electro-optic (EO) phase modulation. Intracavity gain compensates for round-trip losses, sustaining repeated phase modulation and enabling flat-top comb spectra with a 20-dB bandwidth exceeding 1.8 THz. Harmonic-order selection provides widely tunable repetition rates from approximately 5 to 0.2 GHz without substantially compromising the spectral bandwidth. The comb phase noise closely follows that of the radio-frequency (RF) drive at low offset frequencies. Without active frequency stabilization, the two combs exhibit an instrument-limited beat-note linewidth of 2 Hz, indicating high mutual coherence. The generated dual combs enable high-speed DCS at the single-interferogram rate, providing a platform for dynamic spectroscopic measurements. This all-fiber architecture, together with its simplified operation, offers a promising route towards compact and readily integrable dual-comb instruments.
